components.note: 攵 (a hand with a stick) — 教 relates to instructing or disciplining, the traditional action of teaching.
孝 (xiào) gives a hint of the sound — 教 is pronounced jiào, a connection that has shifted somewhat.
育 depicts a woman's body with a baby ⺼ (flesh) growing within — giving 育 its meaning 'to give birth to, to raise, to educate.'

example.hanzi: 每个孩子都应该接受良好的教育。
example.pinyin: Měi gè háizi dōu yīnggāi jiēshòu liánghǎo de jiàoyù.
example.english: Every child should receive a good education.
example.fact: 教育 combines 教 ("to teach", from a hand with a stick disciplining a child) and 育 (a mother's body with a baby growing inside, "to raise, to nurture") — literally "to teach and nurture," reflecting how the word covers both instruction and upbringing, not just schooling.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 谎 describes false speech, a lie.
荒 (huāng) gives the sound — an exact match with 谎, differing only in tone.
口 (mouth) — with strokes above depicting a tongue sticking out — the image of speaking, the source of 言's meaning 'speech, words, language.'

example.hanzi: 他说的都是谎言。
example.pinyin: Tā shuō de dōu shì huǎngyán.
example.english: Everything he said is a lie.
example.fact: 谎言 pairs 谎 ("lie", speech radical 讠 plus phonetic 荒, an exact sound match differing only in tone) with 言 ("words, speech") — literally "lying words." It names the lie itself as a noun; the everyday verb "to lie" is instead the fixed phrase 说谎, not 说谎言.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — encountering someone often happens while moving or traveling.
禺 (yú) gives a sound close to yù, with the tone shifted.
冂 (a simplified eye shape in 见's modern form) — emphasizes the act of seeing.
儿 (a person) — a person with an emphasized eye above gives 见 its meaning 'to see.'

example.hanzi: 我在路上遇见了一个老朋友。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zài lù shàng yùjiàn le yí gè lǎo péngyou.
example.english: I ran into an old friend on the way.
example.fact: 遇见 stresses an unplanned, chance encounter — 遇 alone already means "to run into, to encounter" — unlike 见面, which implies a planned or mutual meeting, so 遇见 rarely appears in sentences like "let's meet at 3pm."

components.note: 耳 is a simplified picture of the outer shape of a human ear.
木 (tree) at the bottom is the plant the flowers grow from.
几 above represents a blossom or cluster of flowers atop the tree, giving 朵 its use as a classifier for flowers and clouds.

example.hanzi: 小狗的耳朵很大。
example.pinyin: Xiǎo gǒu de ěrduo hěn dà.
example.english: The puppy's ears are very big.
example.fact: 朵 is ordinarily a measure word for flowers and clouds (一朵花, "a flower"; 一朵云, "a cloud") — pairing it with 耳 ("ear") to spell "ear" is a soft, almost affectionate image, likening the shape of an ear to a small blossom.

components.note: 世 depicts three leaves or shoots on a stem, suggesting continuous growth across generations — giving rise to the meaning 'generation' or 'world.'
A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.

example.hanzi: 世上没有十全十美的人。
example.pinyin: Shìshàng méiyǒu shí quán shí měi de rén.
example.english: There is no one in the world who is perfect in every way.
example.fact: 世上 is a shortened form of the fuller 世界上 ("in the world") — dropping 界 keeps the same meaning but leans more literary, which is why it turns up often in set phrases and sayings like 世上无难事 ("nothing in this world is too hard") rather than in everyday chit-chat.

components.note: 艹 (grass) — 葬 pictures a burial taking place under the grass.
死 (death, corpse) contributes to the character's form, naming who is being laid to rest.
廾 (two hands) shows the corpse being carefully laid down, completing the picture behind 葬's meaning 'to bury.'
礻 (spirit, altar) — 礼 relates to ceremony and rites performed before the spirits.
乚 reflects the character's phonetic root, though its exact link to the modern reading lǐ is unclear today.

example.hanzi: 我们明天要去参加葬礼。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen míngtiān yào qù cānjiā zànglǐ.
example.english: We are going to attend a funeral tomorrow.
example.fact: 葬 pictures a body being laid down among grass by two hands (艹 grass, 死 corpse, 廾 two hands) — a fairly direct image of burial — while 礼 (from 礻, "altar, ritual") adds the sense of ceremony, so 葬礼 literally reads as "burial rite."

components.note: 甘 (sweet) — describes the fruit's taste.
木 (tree) — the sweet fruit of an unspecified tree gave 某 its meaning 'a certain, some.'
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.

example.hanzi: 据说某人对这件事很不满意。
example.pinyin: Jùshuō mǒurén duì zhè jiàn shì hěn bù mǎnyì.
example.english: I heard a certain person is quite unhappy about this matter.
example.fact: 某人 deliberately withholds identity — sometimes because the speaker genuinely doesn't know who, but often in conversation because they know exactly who and are being coy or indirect about naming them, much like English "someone" said with a knowing look.

meanings: urban area (as opposed to the countryside)

components.note: 土 (earth) — relates to 城's meaning 'city, wall,' since city walls were built of earth.
成 (chéng) gives the sound — 城 is also pronounced chéng, an exact match.
田 (farmland) over 土 (earth/soil) — originally referred to a village or a measured unit of farmland, later extended to mean 'inside' or a unit of distance.

example.hanzi: 他从农村搬到城里工作。
example.pinyin: Tā cóng nóngcūn bān dào chénglǐ gōngzuò.
example.english: He moved from the countryside to the city for work.
example.fact: 城里 pairs 城 ("city, city wall") with 里 ("inside") to literally mean "inside the city walls" — a phrase that still carries a faint echo of the era when Chinese cities were physically walled, so being 城里 meant being inside the wall, as opposed to 城外 or the surrounding countryside.

components.note: 贝 (shell/money — cowrie shells were historically used as currency) — 员 originally related to counting or officials responsible for accounts, later broadening to mean 'member' or 'personnel.'
人 (people) over 云 (clouds/say) — a picture of people gathering and speaking together, related to 会's meanings 'to meet' and 'to know how to.'

example.hanzi: 学校成立了一个新的委员会。
example.pinyin: Xuéxiào chénglì le yí gè xīn de wěiyuánhuì.
example.english: The school established a new committee.
example.fact: 委员会 breaks down as 委员 ("committee member", from 委 "to entrust" plus 员 "member, personnel") plus 会 ("assembly") — literally "an assembly of entrusted members," a fairly transparent path from "a person entrusted with a duty" to "the body such people form."

components.note: 木 (wood) — 机 originally referred to a wooden device or machine, such as a loom.
几 depicts a small table or stool — combined with 木 (wood), the character pictured a wooden machine or mechanism.
木 (wood) — 构 relates to building structures, originally from wooden framing
勾 (gōu) gives a sound close to 构's reading gòu

example.hanzi: 这家机构专门帮助失业的人。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā jīgòu zhuānmén bāngzhù shīyè de rén.
example.english: This organization specializes in helping unemployed people.
example.fact: 机构 combines 机 ("machine, mechanism") with 构 ("to construct, structure") — its earliest use centered on the physical mechanism of a device, with the abstract sense of an organization's "structure" emerging later, the same shift English makes when calling a bureaucracy a "machine."

components.note: 禾 (grain) — 程 originally named a unit for measuring grain, extended to 'process, journey, degree.'
呈 (chéng) gives the sound — 程 is also pronounced chéng, an exact match.
广 (a building or shelter) — 度 pictures people gathering indoors.
廿 (twenty) — a group of people meeting to measure or deliberate gave 度 its meaning of a 'degree' or 'measure,' as in temperature or angles.

example.hanzi: 他对中文的了解已经达到了很高的程度。
example.pinyin: Tā duì Zhōngwén de liǎojiě yǐjīng dádào le hěn gāo de chéngdù.
example.english: His understanding of Chinese has already reached a very high level.
example.fact: 程 originally named a fixed unit for measuring grain before broadening to mean "a measured stage, a journey" (as in 过程, "process") — 程度 keeps that measuring sense alive, pairing it with 度 ("a measure, degree") to describe how far along or how much of something there is.

components.note: 衤 (clothing) — 裙 names a garment, a skirt.
君 (jūn) gives a sound close to qún, sharing the rhyme with a different initial.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 她穿着一条红色的裙子。
example.pinyin: Tā chuānzhe yì tiáo hóngsè de qúnzi.
example.english: She is wearing a red skirt.
example.fact: 裙子 takes the measure word 条 (used for long, narrow things like ropes and rivers) rather than the default 个 — a reminder that many everyday nouns have their own dedicated classifier that a learner has to memorize alongside the noun itself.

components.note: 卩 (a kneeling figure) — a hungry person kneeling down, about to eat.
皀 (a bowl of food) — the meal in front of them, giving 即 its sense of imminent action, 'right away, that is to say.'
丬 (a stylized bed) — 将 originally pictured someone preparing for bed at night.
夕 (evening/night) — the coming of night was seen as predictable, giving 将 its meaning 'about to' or 'going to' happen.

example.hanzi: 春节即将来临。
example.pinyin: Chūnjié jíjiāng láilín.
example.english: The Spring Festival is about to arrive.
example.fact: 即将 is a formal, written-register way to say "about to" — its component 即 alone already means "right away" (from a kneeling person, 卩, in front of a bowl of food, 皀, about to eat) — while casual speech reaches instead for 快要 or 马上 to express the same imminent sense.

components.note: Metal — 钻 relates to a metal tool, a drill.
Gives the sound zhàn, related to zuān but drifted apart over time.
口 (a rock) — the boulder itself.
厂 (a cliff) — the rock lying at the base of a cliff, the source of 石's meaning 'stone, rock.'

example.hanzi: 她的婚戒上镶着一颗钻石。
example.pinyin: Tā de hūnjiè shàng xiāng zhe yì kē zuànshí.
example.english: There is a diamond set in her wedding ring.
example.fact: 钻 as a standalone verb (zuān) means "to drill, to bore through" — a diamond's extreme hardness has long made it the tool of choice for cutting other stones, so 钻石 literally names the gem by what it's used for rather than by its sparkle.

components.note: 爫 (a hand, from above) — 受 pictures something being passed.
又 (a hand, from below) — one hand giving and another receiving gave 受 its meaning 'to receive' or 'to endure.'
The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
Depicts a child wrapped in swaddling, related to 子 (child); the picture-meaning has nothing to do with its modern grammatical role marking a completed action or change of state.

example.hanzi: 这里的天气太热了,我实在受不了。
example.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de tiānqì tài rè le, wǒ shízài shòubuliǎo.
example.english: The weather here is so hot, I really can't stand it.
example.fact: 受不了 is built from 受 ("to bear, to receive") plus the negative potential infix 不 and complement 了 ("manage to") — literally "cannot manage to bear it." Swapping in 得 for 不 gives its positive twin 受得了 ("can bear it"), the same V+得/不+了 pattern behind many Chinese verb complements, like 吃得了 / 吃不了 ("can/can't finish eating").

components.note: 艮 (stubborn, hard) shows 艰 relates to something difficult.
堇 (jǐn) gives a sound close to jiān, sharing the initial consonant.
又 (a hand) — reaching out to try to catch something.
隹 (a bird) — catching a bird by hand is hard, giving 难 its meaning 'difficult.'

example.hanzi: 公司正经历一段艰难的时期。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī zhèng jīnglì yí duàn jiānnán de shíqī.
example.english: The company is going through a difficult period.
example.fact: 艰 and 难 are near-synonyms both meaning "difficult" — 难 is the common, everyday word for "hard," while 艰 mostly appears locked inside compounds (艰苦, 艰巨, 艰难) and rarely stands alone, so pairing it with the more familiar 难 helps anchor its meaning.

meanings: (of a matter) to be determined by

components.note: 土 (earth/soil) — 在 originally related to standing on the ground
才 (cái) gives the sound — 在 is pronounced zài, a close match

example.hanzi: 成功的关键在于坚持不懈。
example.pinyin: Chénggōng de guānjiàn zàiyú jiānchí bú xiè.
example.english: The key to success lies in persisting without giving up.
example.fact: 在于 splits into 在 ("at, located in") and 于 (a more literary preposition largely restricted to formal or written Chinese) — the word is essentially 在 reinforced by its own classical-register cousin, which is why 在于 sounds noticeably more formal than a casual alternative like 主要是 ("mainly is").

components.note: 攵 (a hand with a stick) — 教 relates to instructing or disciplining, the traditional action of teaching.
孝 (xiào) gives a hint of the sound — 教 is pronounced jiào, a connection that has shifted somewhat.
讠 (speech) — 训 relates to teaching through spoken instruction.
川 (chuān) gives a sound distantly related to xùn, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 这次失败给了他一个深刻的教训。
example.pinyin: Zhè cì shībài gěi le tā yí gè shēnkè de jiàoxun.
example.english: This failure gave him a profound lesson.
example.fact: 教训 does double duty as noun ("a lesson learned the hard way") and verb ("to lecture, to scold") — a parent who 教训s a child is literally "teaching-instructing" them, and the noun sense narrowed over time to specifically mean a lesson learned through hardship, not a classroom lesson (that's 课).

components.note: 土 (earth) — 坦 describes flat, level ground.
旦 (dàn) gives a sound close to tǎn, sharing a related rhyme.
Originally depicted a burning candle or the sun's rays radiating outward — the source of 白's meaning 'white, bright, clear.'

example.hanzi: 他向警察坦白了一切。
example.pinyin: Tā xiàng jǐngchá tǎnbái le yíqiè.
example.english: He confessed everything to the police.
example.fact: 坦白 combines 坦 ("flat, level ground") with 白 ("clear, plain, white") — literally "level and clear," a fitting image for a confession that lays everything out openly rather than hiding anything.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — relates to 议's meaning 'to discuss, deliberate; opinion.'
义 (yì) gives the sound — 议 is also pronounced yì, an exact match.
贝 (shell/money — cowrie shells were historically used as currency) — 员 originally related to counting or officials responsible for accounts, later broadening to mean 'member' or 'personnel.'

example.hanzi: 这位议员在演讲中提出了新的提案。
example.pinyin: Zhè wèi yìyuán zài yǎnjiǎng zhōng tíchū le xīn de tí'àn.
example.english: This legislator raised a new proposal during the speech.
example.fact: 议 means "to discuss, to deliberate" (its phonetic component 义 is an exact sound match), and 员 marks a member of a body or profession, as in 演员 ("actor") or 店员 ("shopkeeper") — 议员 literally names "a member of the deliberating body," i.e. a lawmaker.

components.note: 入 (enter, put away) — 全 pictures something being placed into safekeeping.
玉 (jade) — a valuable treasure kept whole and undamaged, giving 全 its meaning of 'complete' or 'entire.'
囗 (a boundary/enclosure) surrounding 玉 (jade, treasure) — a country pictured as protected, valuable territory.

example.hanzi: 这条新闻传遍了全国。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo xīnwén chuánbiàn le quánguó.
example.english: This news spread across the whole country.
example.fact: 全 (from 入 "enter" plus 玉 "jade" — a treasure kept whole and undamaged) prefixes 国 ("country") to mean "the entire nation" — the same 全 + [noun] pattern reappears in this batch's own 全世界 ("the whole world"), showing how productive 全 is as a totality prefix.

components.note: 心 (heart) — 慈 describes a warm, kind-hearted feeling toward others.
兹 (zī) shares the rhyme -i with cí, and both use dental sibilant initials (c/z) — only the aspiration and tone differ.
羊 (sheep) — food offered generously to another person
口 (mouth) — kind words spoken alongside the gift

example.hanzi: 她把大部分收入都捐给了慈善机构。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ dàbùfen shōurù dōu juān gěi le císhàn jīgòu.
example.english: She donated most of her income to charitable organizations.
example.fact: 慈善 almost always shows up attached to a following noun — 慈善机构 ("charity organization"), 慈善晚会 ("charity gala") — rather than standing alone for "charity" itself, which is instead 慈善事业 ("the charity cause") or, in casual speech, simply 捐款 ("donation").

components.note: 食 (food) — 餐 relates directly to eating and meals.
饣 (food) points to a place where meals are served.
官 pictures an official hall or residence, giving 馆 its sense of a large public building.

example.hanzi: 我们晚上去那家新开的餐馆吃饭吧。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen wǎnshang qù nà jiā xīn kāi de cānguǎn chīfàn ba.
example.english: Let's go eat at that newly opened restaurant tonight.
example.fact: 餐馆 is one of several near-synonyms for "restaurant" alongside 饭店 and 饭馆 — 餐馆 leans slightly more formal or Western in flavor (西餐馆, "Western restaurant"), while 饭店 in Mainland usage can also mean "hotel," a common trap for learners who assume it always means "restaurant."

components.note: 罒 (net) — relates to 罗's original meaning 'net for catching birds,' extended to 'to gather, collect' and used today as a common Chinese surname.
马 (simplified from 馬) depicts a horse in profile, with its mane, legs, and tail visible — later simplified into just a few strokes.

example.hanzi: 罗马是意大利的首都。
example.pinyin: Luómǎ shì Yìdàlì de shǒudū.
example.english: Rome is the capital of Italy.
example.fact: 罗马 is a phonetic transliteration with no real connection to its characters' own meanings (罗 "net," 马 "horse") — the characters were picked purely for their sound, the same strategy Chinese uses for most foreign place names.

components.note: A drawing of a hand peeling the hide away from an animal.
Flesh — skin is part of the body.
Gives the sound fū, matching the character's reading.

example.hanzi: 冬天皮肤很容易干燥。
example.pinyin: Dōngtiān pífū hěn róngyì gānzào.
example.english: Skin easily gets dry in winter.
example.fact: 皮 alone already means "skin, hide, peel" and applies broadly to people, animals, or fruit alike (苹果皮, "apple peel") — 肤 narrows that general sense specifically to human skin, so 皮肤 fuses a broad root word with a person-specific modifier.

components.note: 阝 (a variant of 邑, meaning place/settlement) — 部 relates to a division, section, or department.
咅 supplies the sound for 部 (bù); it belongs to the same phonetic family as related characters like 倍 (bèi) and 培 (péi).
阝 (a mound or place) — 队 pictures people gathering together.
人 (person) — people gathering in one place gave 队 its meaning 'a team' or 'a line/queue.'

example.hanzi: 他去年参加了部队。
example.pinyin: Tā qùnián cānjiā le bùduì.
example.english: He joined the army last year.
example.fact: 部队 literally combines 部 ("division, section") with 队 ("team, line") — a division organized into ranks — and doubles today as informal shorthand for "the military" in general, much as English speakers say "the army" to mean military service broadly.

components.note: 匸 (an enclosure or boundary) — 区 pictures a defined territory.
乂 (a mark, here representing control or division) — dividing land into bounded territories gave 区 its meaning 'district' or 'area.'
另 (other, separate) — 别 relates to distinguishing one thing from another.
刂 (knife) — cutting things apart to sort them gave 别 its meaning 'to separate' or 'other,' and later, 'don't' as a command.

example.hanzi: 这两个词的区别是什么?
example.pinyin: Zhè liǎng gè cí de qūbié shì shénme?
example.english: What's the difference between these two words?
example.fact: 区别 works as both noun ("a difference") and verb ("to distinguish, to tell apart") without changing form at all — a common pattern in Chinese, where the same two-character compound flexibly serves different parts of speech depending on where it lands in the sentence.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh/body) — 背 refers to the back, a part of the body
北 (běi) gives a sound close to 背's reading bèi, sharing a similar historical pronunciation

example.hanzi: 他总是在背后说别人的坏话。
example.pinyin: Tā zǒngshì zài bèihòu shuō biéren de huàihuà.
example.english: He always talks badly about people behind their backs.
example.fact: 背后 extends its literal spatial sense ("behind, at the back") into the same figurative territory as the English idiom "behind someone's back" — talking about someone 背后 implies secrecy or gossip, a metaphor the two languages happen to share almost exactly.

components.note: 衣 (clothing) — 装 relates to clothes, dress, and attire
壮 (zhuàng) gives the sound — 装 is pronounced zhuāng, a close match
罒 (a net) — 置 originally meant to set a net in place
直 (zhí) gives a sound close to 置's reading zhì, sharing a similar historical pronunciation

example.hanzi: 这台机器上装有一个安全装置。
example.pinyin: Zhè tái jīqì shàng zhuāng yǒu yí gè ānquán zhuāngzhì.
example.english: This machine has a safety device installed on it.
example.fact: 装置 covers both noun ("a device, apparatus") and verb ("to install, to set up"). 装 originally centered on dress and attire (its 衣 "clothing" component) but has drifted to also mean "to install" or even "to pretend," while 置 ("to place, to put") reinforces the placement sense that 装置 relies on today.

components.note: 入 (enter, put away) — 全 pictures something being placed into safekeeping.
玉 (jade) — a valuable treasure kept whole and undamaged, giving 全 its meaning of 'complete' or 'entire.'
世 depicts three leaves or shoots on a stem, suggesting continuous growth across generations — giving rise to the meaning 'generation' or 'world.'
田 (field) — relates to 界's original meaning, the boundary line between farm fields.
介 (jiè) gives the sound — 界 is also pronounced jiè, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 这种病毒已经传播到全世界。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng bìngdú yǐjīng chuánbò dào quánshìjiè.
example.english: This virus has already spread across the entire world.
example.fact: 全世界 stacks two "whole" ideas back to back — 全 ("entire") reinforcing 世界 ("world," itself literally "generations" 世 plus "boundary" 界) — giving the phrase a slightly more emphatic feel than 世界 alone, similar to English occasionally saying "the whole entire world."

components.note: 木 (wood) — 权 originally meant a wooden lever or weight, later extended to 'power, authority, right.'
雚 was historically closer to guàn; the pronunciation has since shifted to quán, so the sound link is faint today.
力 depicts the blade of a plow — since plowing fields took great physical effort, the shape came to represent strength or power.

example.hanzi: 总统的权力受到宪法的限制。
example.pinyin: Zǒngtǒng de quánlì shòudào xiànfǎ de xiànzhì.
example.english: The president's power is limited by the constitution.
example.fact: 权力 ("power, authority") is a common point of confusion with its near-homophone 权利 — identical pinyin and tones, differing only in the second character (力 "force" vs 利 "benefit"), yet naming two entirely different concepts: the capacity to act versus an entitlement one holds.

components.note: 三 is made of three simple horizontal strokes stacked together — the most direct way to picture the number three, following the same pattern as 一 (one) and 二 (two).
日 (sun) — combined with 月 (moon), 明 shows the light of both sun and moon, giving the meaning 'bright' or 'clear.'
月 (moon) — together with 日 (sun), the two brightest things in the sky represent brightness and clarity.
氵 (water) — 治 relates to managing or controlling the flow of water, such as flood control.
台 (a platform, structure) — a structure used to direct and control water gave 治 its meaning 'to govern' or 'to manage.'

example.hanzi: 我午饭吃了一个三明治。
example.pinyin: Wǒ wǔfàn chī le yí gè sānmíngzhì.
example.english: I ate a sandwich for lunch.
example.fact: 三明治 is a phonetic transliteration of English "sandwich" — the characters (三 "three," 明 "bright," 治 "govern") were picked purely for their sound and carry no meaningful connection to the food, the same borrowing strategy seen in 罗马 ("Rome") elsewhere in this batch.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 棒 describes an object made of wood, a stick.
奉 (fèng) gives a sound only distantly related to bàng today, having drifted apart over time.
王 (a variant of 玉, meaning jade) — 球 originally referred to a round piece of jade, extended to mean 'ball, sphere'
求 (qiú) gives the sound — 球 is also pronounced qiú, an exact match

example.hanzi: 他每个周末都去打棒球。
example.pinyin: Tā měi gè zhōumò dōu qù dǎ bàngqiú.
example.english: He goes to play baseball every weekend.
example.fact: 棒球 is a transparent calque of English "baseball" — 棒 ("a stick, a bat") plus 球 ("ball") — translated by meaning rather than sound, unlike the purely phonetic sports and food loanwords elsewhere in this batch (三明治, "sandwich").

components.note: 耳 (ear) — chatting involves listening as well as speaking.
卯 (mǎo) gives a sound distantly related to liáo, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 有空的话,我们聊聊天。
example.pinyin: Yǒu kòng dehuà, wǒmen liáoliao tiān.
example.english: If you have time, let's chat for a bit.
example.fact: 聊聊 reduplicates the single verb 聊 ("to chat") — the same softening pattern seen elsewhere in this deck's 谢谢 (from 谢) — turning a plain verb into a light, casual invitation. In speech it's very often extended to 聊聊天 ("have a little chat"), where 天 functions as a fixed, largely idiomatic object rather than literally meaning "sky."

components.note: 亲 (here representing a tree, related to 榛/hazel) — 新 pictures a tree being cut.
斤 (an axe) — freshly chopping wood gave 新 its meaning of something 'new' or 'fresh.'
鱼 (fish) — 鲜 originally described fresh fish or meat.
羊 (yáng) gives the sound — an exact match with 鲜.

example.hanzi: 这些蔬菜看起来很新鲜。
example.pinyin: Zhèxiē shūcài kàn qǐlai hěn xīnxiān.
example.english: These vegetables look very fresh.
example.fact: 新鲜 combines 新 ("new") with 鲜 (originally "fresh fish or meat," built from 鱼 "fish" plus 羊 "sheep") — 鲜 alone still carries that food-freshness sense (鲜肉, "fresh meat"), which is why 新鲜 extends naturally to non-food senses like a "fresh" or novel idea, mirroring the same metaphor English makes.

components.note: A drawing of a left hand holding a tool, contrasted with 又, an early form of the right hand.

example.hanzi: 会议大概三点左右开始。
example.pinyin: Huìyì dàgài sān diǎn zuǒyòu kāishǐ.
example.english: The meeting will start at around three o'clock.
example.fact: Beyond its literal "left and right," 左右 attached after a number becomes Mandarin's all-purpose "approximately" (三点左右, "around 3 o'clock"; 十个左右, "about ten") — the logic being that the true value sits somewhere between a bit to the left and a bit to the right of the stated number.

components.note: 攵 (a hand with an implement, action) — relates to 放's meaning 'to let go, release, put.'
方 (fāng) gives the sound — 放 is pronounced fàng, a close match sharing the same rhyme.
心 was originally a pictograph of the physical shape of a human heart, and came to represent the mind, feelings, and intention as well.

example.hanzi: 别担心,你可以放心。
example.pinyin: Bié dānxīn, nǐ kěyǐ fàngxīn.
example.english: Don't worry, you can relax.
example.fact: 放心 literally means "to set down (放) the heart-mind (心)" — the same 心 that anchors 担心 ("to carry worry in the heart") and 关心 ("to care") — Chinese frequently locates emotion physically in 心 much the way English locates it in the "heart," which makes 放心 fairly transparent once you know the character.

components.note: 冖 (a covering/roof) — represents the building or schoolhouse where learning happens.
子 (child) — 学 depicts children gathered to study.
⺍ is a small graphic element at the top of the character; its original pictorial meaning, if any, has been lost over time.
人 (people) over 云 (clouds/say) — a picture of people gathering and speaking together, related to 会's meanings 'to meet' and 'to know how to.'

example.hanzi: 我终于学会了怎么用筷子。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zhōngyú xuéhuì le zěnme yòng kuàizi.
example.english: I finally learned how to use chopsticks.
example.fact: 学会 pairs 学 ("to study") with 会 in its complement sense "to have mastered, to know how to." 学会 specifically marks the moment a skill is acquired, contrasted with plain 学 (ongoing study) or 会 alone (already knowing how). The same two characters, read as a noun instead, separately mean "institute, learned society."

components.note: 疒 (sickness) — a scar is a mark left by an injury or illness.
艮 (gèn) gives a sound close in rhyme to hén, though the initial consonant has drifted.
辶 (to walk) — 迹 names the trace left behind by walking.
亦 (yì) gives a sound distantly related to jī, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 墙上还留着火灾的痕迹。
example.pinyin: Qiáng shàng hái liú zhe huǒzāi de hénjì.
example.english: Traces of the fire are still left on the wall.
example.fact: 痕 (built on 疒, "sickness") originally named a scar left by injury, while 迹 (built on 辶, "to walk") named a footprint or trail left by walking — 痕迹 fuses "scar" and "footprint" into one word for any lingering trace, whether physical damage or a path once taken.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — a heavy, ripe stalk of grain standing steady in the field ties to 稳's meaning 'stable, steady.'
㥯 (wěn) gives the sound — an exact match with 稳's reading wěn.
宀 (roof) — represents a home or fixed dwelling.
疋 (a foot/person) — a person settling down under a roof gave 定 its meaning 'to decide, to fix, to settle.'

example.hanzi: 他现在有一份稳定的工作。
example.pinyin: Tā xiànzài yǒu yí fèn wěndìng de gōngzuò.
example.english: He now has a stable job.
example.fact: 稳 pictures a heavy, ripe stalk of grain (禾) standing firm rather than swaying — 稳定 extends that image of settled grain to anything that holds steady, whether a job, a market, or an emotional state (情绪稳定, "emotionally stable").

components.note: 酋 pictures a jar of wine.
寸 (hand) below offers it up respectfully, giving 尊 its meaning 'to respect, to honor.'

example.hanzi: 我们都很尊敬这位老师。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen dōu hěn zūnjìng zhè wèi lǎoshī.
example.english: We all really respect this teacher.
example.fact: 尊 pictures a jar of wine (酋) offered up with both hands (寸) — a gesture of formal respect toward elders or superiors — while 敬 independently carries the same reverence. 尊敬 is generally reserved for people, whereas the broader 尊重 ("to respect") can also apply to opinions, rules, or feelings.

components.note: 匸 (an enclosure or boundary) — 区 pictures a defined territory.
乂 (a mark, here representing control or division) — dividing land into bounded territories gave 区 its meaning 'district' or 'area.'
土 (earth) — 域 names a bounded area of land, a territory.
或 (huò) reflects the character's historical phonetic root; the modern reading yù has since diverged.

example.hanzi: 这个区域禁止停车。
example.pinyin: Zhège qūyù jìnzhǐ tíngchē.
example.english: Parking is prohibited in this area.
example.fact: 区域 doubles up two near-synonymous "bounded space" characters — 区 (a fenced-off territory) and 域 (a plot of land marked by boundaries, built on 土 "earth") — the same root 区 also anchors 区别 elsewhere in this batch, though there it means "distinction" rather than "territory."

components.note: 弓 (bow) — a strong bow that took great force to draw gave 强 its meaning 'strong, powerful.'
虫 was a different phonetic element historically; its pronunciation has shifted so far from qiáng over time that the sound link is no longer obvious.

example.hanzi: 她在困难面前表现得很坚强。
example.pinyin: Tā zài kùnnan miànqián biǎoxiàn de hěn jiānqiáng.
example.english: She showed great strength in the face of difficulty.
example.fact: 坚强 typically describes inner, emotional or moral strength — a strong-willed person who doesn't break under pressure — while physical strength usually reaches for a different word, 强壮 (of the body) or 有力 (of a grip or force), a distinction English's single adjective "strong" doesn't make.

components.note: 攵 (a hand with a stick, action) — 数 relates to the action of counting.
娄 (lóu) gives a hint of the sound — 数 is pronounced shù, a connection that has drifted over time.
扌 (hand) — relates to 据's meaning 'to rely on, according to,' as if grasping evidence in hand.
居 (jū) gave the base sound; the pronunciation later shifted to jù, keeping the same final but a different tone.

example.hanzi: 这些数据显示销量在上升。
example.pinyin: Zhèxiē shùjù xiǎnshì xiāoliàng zài shàngshēng.
example.english: This data shows that sales are rising.
example.fact: 据 alone means "evidence, basis" (its 扌 "hand" component evokes grasping something as proof) — 数据 literally means "numerical evidence," a word that entered modern Chinese to translate the Western mathematical and statistical concept of "data," later extending naturally to computing.

components.note: Jade — an old semantic group for stone/gem-like materials, including glass.
Gives the sound pí, related to bō but drifted apart over time.
Jade — an old semantic group for stone/gem-like materials, including glass.
Gives the sound lí, matching the character's reading.

example.hanzi: 小心,这个杯子是玻璃做的。
example.pinyin: Xiǎoxīn, zhège bēizi shì bōli zuò de.
example.english: Be careful, this cup is made of glass.
example.fact: 玻璃 is a rare case where both characters share the same 王 (jade) semantic component yet neither carries independent meaning outside this word — 玻 and 璃 exist almost solely to spell "glass," a treatment more typical of foreign loanwords than native vocabulary.

components.note: 力 (strength) — 勇 describes inner strength shown as courage.
甬 (yǒng) is an exact match for the sound of 勇.
气 (simplified from 氣) depicts rising wisps or vapor, like breath or steam drifting upward — a simple picture of air or gas.

example.hanzi: 她终于有勇气告诉父母真相。
example.pinyin: Tā zhōngyú yǒu yǒngqì gàosu fùmǔ zhēnxiàng.
example.english: She finally had the courage to tell her parents the truth.
example.fact: 勇气 pairs 勇 ("brave," built from 力 "strength" plus phonetic 甬, an exact sound match) with 气 ("qi, vital energy") — literally "brave energy," treating courage the way several Chinese compounds treat emotions and mental states: as a form of 气 that can be summoned or run out of (没气了, "out of steam").

components.note: 钅 (metal) — early mirrors were made of polished bronze.
竟 (jìng) is an exact match for the sound of 镜.
大 (big) — in 头's simplified form, this element is linked to the idea of 'high' or topmost, since the head sits at the top of the body.

example.hanzi: 这部电影的第一个镜头拍得非常美。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng de dì yī gè jìngtóu pāi de fēicháng měi.
example.english: The first shot of this movie was filmed beautifully.
example.fact: 镜头 combines 镜 ("mirror," originally polished bronze, 钅) with 头 ("head, tip") — "the tip of the mirror" names the physical lens on a camera, and by extension came to mean an individual filmed shot, the same way English "shot" names both a camera action and its resulting clip.

components.note: 贝 (shell/money — cowrie shells were historically used as currency) — 员 originally related to counting or officials responsible for accounts, later broadening to mean 'member' or 'personnel.'
工 depicts a carpenter's square or workman's tool — a simple shape that came to represent work and labor.

example.hanzi: 公司为员工提供免费午餐。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī wèi yuángōng tígōng miǎnfèi wǔcān.
example.english: The company provides free lunch for its employees.
example.fact: 员工 fuses 员 ("a person holding a role," as in 演员 "actor" or 服务员 "waiter") with 工 ("worker, labor") into a catch-all term covering everyone on a company's payroll, without distinguishing rank the way 职员 (office staff specifically) or 工人 (manual laborer specifically) do.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — 联 originally meant 'connected, linked,' perhaps through the image of joined loops.
关 (guān) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from lián.
皿 (dish) — 盟 originally described an oath sworn over a sacrificial dish.
明 (míng) gives a sound distantly related to méng, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 这两个国家签订了军事联盟。
example.pinyin: Zhè liǎng gè guójiā qiāndìng le jūnshì liánméng.
example.english: These two countries signed a military alliance.
example.fact: 盟 pictures an oath sworn over a sacrificial dish (皿) — an image straight out of ancient Chinese covenant ceremonies — and 联 ("to link, to connect") joins it to name any formal alliance, whether ancient states swearing blood oaths or modern countries signing treaties.

components.note: 阝 (a hillside/place) — the sunlit side of a hill or place
日 (the sun) — the source of light and warmth
儿 (a person) — shown carrying a torch overhead, the source of 光's meaning 'light, brightness.'
火 (fire) — the torch's flame, the thing giving off the light.

example.hanzi: 今天的阳光特别好。
example.pinyin: Jīntiān de yángguāng tèbié hǎo.
example.english: Today's sunshine is especially nice.
example.fact: 阳光 literally means "yang light" — 阳 being the bright, active half of the classical yin-yang (阴阳) pairing — and the word has picked up a modern extension describing an upbeat, warm personality (阳光男孩, "a sunny, positive guy"), the same metaphor English makes when calling someone's disposition "sunny."
